tts: Are you doing anything on Friday night? — No, I don’t think so. Why?
Do you fancy coming round for dinner? — That sounds great. Oh, hang on, did you say Friday?
Yes, is there a problem? — I’m sorry, but I can’t make Friday. I’m meeting a friend from university.
No problem. How about Saturday instead? — Saturday? That’d be great.

tts: Hello, Weber Design Solutions. — Oh hello, Max, this is Seyit Samyeli. I’m sorry I missed your call.
Ah, Seyit, good to hear from you. Thanks for returning my call. — Yes, I’m pleased to hear you’re coming over soon.
Thank you, I’m looking forward to it. Are you free that week at all? — Yes, it’s fine for me.
Great, so would you like to meet for lunch? — Yes, I’d like to very much, thanks. — OK, so how about the twenty-eighth? Is that OK for you?

items.s: Max is going to visit Seyit’s city.

acts.title: Two emails, one lunch
text: Thanks for calling back yesterday — good to speak to you at last.
As I said, I’m in Izmir the week of the 27th and I’d love to meet up while I’m there. Do you fancy lunch?
How about Wednesday the 28th, around one? There’s a place on the seafront that everybody recommends. If Wednesday doesn’t work, I’m free on Thursday morning as well.
Let me know what suits you and I’ll book a table.
Wednesday the 28th works for me. Shall we say one o’clock at the seafront place? I know the one you mean.
One small thing: I have a meeting until half past twelve on the other side of town, so I might be five minutes late. Please start without me if I am.
Looking forward to it. See you on the 28th.

write.q: Write an invitation email and the reply: about 6 lines each. Follow the model’s six moves — thank them, say when you are around, invite, suggest a day, time and place, offer a second option, say what you will do next. In the reply, accept, fix the exact time, and mention one small practical detail.
write.model: Hi Marat, Thanks for the message on Tuesday — good to hear from you at last. I’m in Astana the week of the 14th and I’d love to meet while I’m there. Do you fancy dinner? How about Thursday the 17th, around seven? There’s a place near the station that everybody talks about. If Thursday doesn’t work, I’m free on Friday evening as well. Let me know what suits you and I’ll book a table. Best, Aigul — Hi Aigul, Thursday the 17th works for me. Shall we say half past seven instead of seven? I finish at six on the other side of town. Looking forward to it. See you on the 17th. Marat

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: invite somebody, hear that the first day doesn’t work, offer a second day, agree the exact time, and say you’ll confirm by email.
speak.model: Are you doing anything on Friday night? Do you fancy coming round for dinner? — I’m sorry, but I can’t make Friday. — How about Saturday instead? — Saturday works for me. — Shall we say seven? I’ll confirm by email tomorrow.
